title: Report the day's slow requests without queueing on the dashboard

blocks.text: Every night the platform team scans the day's request latencies for requests slower than the service's target and adds them to the operations dashboard's `Tally`. The `Tally` is shared by the whole scan and takes a lock on every `report(...)` call. On a busy day the scan is slow, and a profile shows the pool's workers spending most of their time waiting for that lock.
Finish `scanHere()` of the `Scan` task in `src/main/java/practice/SlowRequests.java`. It handles one part of the day, on the current thread. When you're done:

items: the tally gains exactly the slow requests of the day and the milliseconds they took, on top of whatever earlier scans reported;
the scan's workers spend as little time on the tally's lock as the totals allow: the dashboard shows `reports()`, how many times the lock was taken.

cases.says: the tally gains exactly the day's slow requests and their milliseconds, on top of what it already held, for any day and threshold
each part of the scan counts on its own and reports to the shared tally once, not once per slow request

origin.section: Leaves Count Locally and Add to the Shared Total Once

concepts: Leaves that add to one shared total count locally and add to it once per leaf, rather than once per element.
